author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
Arm touches, laughs, and firm handshakes were on display as Chinese President Xi Jinping and his American counterpart Donald Trump began their high-stakes summit in Washington, which has so far featured a rare airport welcome, military pageantry and closed-door bilateral talks.
While the outcomes of the pair’s discussions are being closely watched, so are the exchanges between the leaders of the world’s two largest economies. A body language expert who reviewed the interactions said Trump’s...
title: Pat on the back? Xi and Trump’s body language speaks volumes

author: Han Li
description:
Melania Trump and China’s first lady Peng Liyuan toured Chinese artworks and a room shaped by Asian design at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art in Washington on Thursday, as their husbands held talks at the White House.
The museum’s director, Chase Robinson, said the two women spent about 45 minutes there and were “full of questions”. Much of the visit centred on the Peacock Room, whose displays of Chinese porcelain made it a fitting setting for the occasion, he said.
“What better...
title: Inside Melania Trump and Peng Liyuan’s visit to the Smithsonian’s Peacock Room

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
When the presidents of the United States and China meet in Washington, the world will be watching to see whether their two countries can make good on their agreement to work towards “constructive strategic stability”. In the sixth part of a series, Khushboo Razdan looks at how a presidential appeal to America’s heartland is playing out.
Of the countless preparations being made for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s highly anticipated American trip, arguably the first came in the form of a personal...
title: What Xi Jinping’s letter to old friends in Iowa means in a struggling, altered America

author: Wang Huiyao
description:
The European Commission is pressing China for progress by next month to address the widening EU-China trade imbalance, and raising the possibility of new protectionist trade policy. The deadline raises a question: how should China and its trading partners address perceived economic imbalances while sharing the benefits of Chinese industrial competitiveness?
China’s merchandise trade surplus approached US$1.2 trillion last year even as other exporting economies press for controls. “Overcapacity”...
title: China’s industrial strengths must also benefit its trading partners

author: Dewey Sim,Ji Siqi,Vincent Chow
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his American counterpart Donald Trump delivered remarks at the White House on Thursday morning at the start of the second day of Xi’s closely watched state visit.
Both leaders spoke warmly of their countries’ ties and pledged deeper cooperation in comments that sought to project an image of stability between the two sides.
Trump said he and Xi would work together to build a “better future for both our countries” while Xi called for the two powers to “coexist in...
title: B-2 Spirit, AI cooperation, no US-China conflict: key Xi-Trump takeaways so far

author: Mark Magnier
description:
After weeks of frustration, delays and posturing, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump got down to business on Thursday, kicking off their high-stakes summit, Xi’s first on US soil since 2015.
The two started the morning with a formal arrival ceremony on the White House South Lawn and Rose Garden that included nearly 500 military personnel, the Chinese and American national anthems played by the US Marine Band and opening remarks from both leaders.
Both leaders sought to...
title: Beyond the Rose Garden and the military review, Trump and Xi get down to business

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China’s next aircraft carrier could be longer than the US Navy’s largest warship, according to new satellite images that offer fresh clues about how far from home Beijing intends to operate its fleet – and the logistics it will need to do so.
Captured on September 4, the images show that work has begun on the bulbous bow of the carrier under construction at Dalian Shipyard in northeastern China, defence intelligence company Janes reported last week.
Measurements from the stern to the projected...
title: China’s next carrier could be its longest – what are Beijing’s plans?

author: Khushboo Razdan,William Zheng,Nayan Seth
description:
A small group of Chinese CEOs holding US visas has arrived in Washington after travelling separately from President Xi Jinping’s official entourage, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
But with the clock ticking and the business optics of the Chinese leader’s White House visit hanging on the final twists of diplomatic negotiations, the executives are still waiting to find out whether they will secure a seat at Thursday’s state dinner for Xi.
“Beijing’s security protocol is...
title: Chinese CEOs fly to US on own, await invites to Trump’s state dinner for Xi Jinping

author: Fan Chen
description:
Starkly contrasting receptions for the Japanese leader and the Chinese president in the United States have sparked debate over Washington’s treatment of Tokyo as an ally.
Sanae Takaichi arrived in New York at the start of the working week, beginning a trip where she addressed the United Nations General Assembly for the first time as the country’s prime minister.
A photo taken on her arrival shows her waving across a relatively empty tarmac at John F. Kennedy International Airport. Footage...
title: Red carpet vs empty tarmac: Xi’s US welcome fuels debate over Takaichi’s no-show reception

author: Caroline Lin
description:
American tenor Christopher Macchio will perform at the White House banquet for Chinese President Xi Jinping during his first state visit to the United States in more than a decade.
“An honour to return to Washington DC to perform for the State Dinner with Donald Trump (originally @realDonaldTrump) and President Xi,” Macchio said on social media, tagging the official accounts of Trump, the White House, and the Trump campaign.
Often referred to as “America’s Tenor”, Macchio is a...
title: US tenor Christopher Macchio booked for Xi-Trump state dinner performance

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China’s first lady Peng Liyuan has sparked online buzz over her English-language exchanges with the US first lady without an interpreter during her visit to Washington with President Xi Jinping this week.
On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump greeted Xi and Peng at Joint Base Andrews in a rare diplomatic move.
After Xi and Peng stepped off the plane, the two couples spoke with the help of interpreters.


But as they walked along the red carpet, Peng and Melania...
title: First lady Peng Liyuan’s English takes the spotlight in exchange with Melania Trump

author: Carol Yang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US is his first to the country since 2023 and his eighth face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump. From informal walk-and-talks to a state dinner, Xi’s meetings across four American administrations show how personal rapport and official diplomacy reflect the growing complexity of US-China relations.
Xi’s first US visit as president: a shirtsleeves summit
In June 2013, just months after assuming the presidency, Xi travelled to the United States following...
title: Summits for all diplomatic seasons: how the US has set the stage for Xi Jinping

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
China and the United States agreed to extend a trade-war truce by two months to January 10, as President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington for a summit with US President Donald Trump.
The short extension will let the US assess whether China is meeting trade commitments, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday following “unscheduled” extra talks with Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng. China had sought to stretch the “Busan Agreement” pause until January 2029, when Trump’s term in...
title: US, China agree two-month trade truce extension ahead of summit

author: Fan Chen
description:
China and the United States must prevent their AI competition from escalating into a cold war, a top Chinese policy adviser has warned, while asserting that a complete decoupling would be difficult.
The remarks from Zheng Yongnian, a leading political scientist and dean of the school of public policy at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, come ahead of the Xi-Trump summit in Washington, where artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to be among the top items on the agenda.
Chinese...
title: American AI development ‘cannot separate itself from China’: Zheng Yongnian

author: Nicholas Spiro
description:
As Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his much-anticipated summit with US President Donald Trump, it is clear which country emerged stronger from the tariff shock. Last month, China’s exports rose 25 per cent in annualised terms, causing the country’s trade surplus to swell to US$119 billion and putting it on track to exceed last year’s record of US$1.2 trillion.
Moreover, China’s surplus with the US rose 44 per cent to US$29 billion, the widest gap since Trump returned to...
title: Who has the upper hand in financial markets, the US or China?

author: Albee Zhang
description:
At Joint Base Andrews where Donald Trump rolled out the red carpet for the visiting Chinese president, Xi Jinping appeared unfazed during a ceremonial flyover by a screeching US bomber while the US president visibly winced at the noise.
As Xi arrived at the military base just outside Washington, he was greeted with a ceremony that included the US Air Force band playing the American and Chinese national anthems, a 21-gun salute, a guard of honour, a display of six F-16 and six F-22 fighter jets,...
title: Trump grimaces, Xi unfazed during US military flyover for historic tarmac welcome

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
US President Donald Trump’s choice of attire at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday drew online attention as he made a rare personal appearance to welcome Xi Jinping.
Trump was on the tarmac to greet Xi on Wednesday evening as the Chinese president arrived in Washington for his first US state visit in more than a decade.
But while temperatures at the airbase were around 19 degrees Celsius (66 Fahrenheit), Trump was the only one wearing a dark overcoat and gloves as he and first lady Melania Trump...
title: Why did Trump wear gloves to greet China’s Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews?

author: Shi Huang
description:
Chinese medical scientists have shattered the brief window of time available to limit stroke damage, effectively shielding injured brain cells and dramatically improving the odds of a full recovery.
Brain cells start dying within minutes of a clot blocking an artery, leading to facial droop, affected speech and in severe cases, paralysis or death. Emergency treatments, such as clot-busting drugs or surgery, must be given within a maximum of six hours.
According to a study published by the...
title: Chinese drug Loberamisal extends stroke treatment window from 6 hours to 2 days

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
A video clip showing uniformed US military personnel on their hands and knees making last-minute adjustments to a red carpet has gone viral online, as President Donald Trump rolled out a lavish welcome for his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews.
The 12-second clip, which circulated widely on US social media, captured several service members hurriedly smoothing and cleaning the 30-metre (98 feet) carpet moments before Xi emerged from his aircraft.


Chinese officials – including...
title: Video of US military adjusting red carpet for China’s Xi sparks online backlash

author: Carol Yang
description:
With the balance of power shifting between the US and China, the success of this week’s summit hinges not on headline-grabbing deals, but on practical, cautious consensus under a new strategic stability framework, according to Chinese researchers.
Media outlets in China have given heavy coverage to President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the United States, highlighting its “historic, milestone significance”. It follows US President Donald Trump’s Beijing visit in May.
Xi’s arrival in Washington on...
title: Big picture or big deals? What the Xi-Trump summit holds for China and the US

author: Lijia Zhang
description:
“Whoever wins with AI wins,” US President Donald Trump has declared, dismissing warnings about the risks of developing artificial intelligence too rapidly and citing rivalry with China.
The technological competition is real. China has reason to fear becoming dependent on America for advanced chips and AI technology, particularly as Washington has repeatedly restricted its access to cutting-edge semiconductors. China, meanwhile, is directing enormous resources towards AI. Stanford University’s...
title: China’s top priority should be wages, not AI

author: Holly Chik
description:
While major powers compete in militarised space races and state-led megaprojects, a group comprising a Russian astronaut trainer, Chinese science educators and Malaysian collaborators is laying the groundwork for an international youth space camp.
Set to be held in Penang’s rainforest eco-park in late 2027 at the earliest, the week-long programme will gather youth from around the region to inspire future spacefarers, scientists and global citizens through physical exercises, immersion in space...
title: China-Russia space camp in Malaysia opens to youth in Southeast Asia

author: Holly Chik,Lucy Quaggin
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping was greeted on the tarmac by his American counterpart Donald Trump on Wednesday – a rare gesture ahead of their summit. It is Xi’s first state visit to the United States in over a decade and the two leaders met each other at Joint Base Andrews just after 6pm, alongside their wives Melania Trump and Peng Liyuan. Here are the key takeaways.
1. Trade truce extended
As Xi and Peng touched down in America, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News that the two...
title: Warm welcome, trade truce extended: the takeaways as Xi arrives in US
